To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the measurement of TAFIA and the activation peptide is superior to the measurement of total TAFI for the investigation of TAFI and atherosclerosis.
ELISAs were developed that measure the extent of activation of TAFI, and that the extent of activation was increased in subjects with hyperlipidaemia.
the measurement of TAFIs activation state by ELISA constitutes an improved method for studying the relationship between plasma levels of TAFI and various cardiovascular disorders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods that allow to quantify TAFI antigen and TAFI activity in plasma samples.
the development and application of novel assays for measuring the extent of plasma TAFI activation in relation to cardiovascular risk.
the development and application of new methods to measure TAFI activation, and to study the relationship between TFI activation, cardiovascular disease and hyperlipidemia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the measurement of the extent of activation of TAFI is more sensitive in the study of the relationship between TFI and cardiovascular diseases.
TAFI activation is increased in hyperlipidemic subjects, which may be a contributing factor in the pathophysiology of hyperlipidemia.
the TAFI activation assays developed in the current study provide a sensitive and specific tool for the analysis of the activation status of TAFI and its role in cardiovascular disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ELISAs for the measurement of the extent of TFI activation can be used for the detection of TFI activation in vitro, in vivo, and ex vivo, and that these ELISAs constitute a more sensitive tool for the detection of the extent of activation than ELISAs for total TFI antigen levels.
we have developed ELISAs that measure the extent of the activation of the TAFI system.
the activation peptide is a more sensitive marker of cardiovascular disease than TAFI or TAFIa.

the development of ELISAs that allow measuring the activation of TAFI is feasible.
